newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Cargolux had 90.2 pct load factor in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Cargolux had 90.2 pct load factor in 1996.

text.p: Cargolux Airlines International said overall cargo load factor in 1996 totalled 90.2 percent compared to 89.4 percent in 1995.
Cargolux operates a fleet of three Boeing 747-400Fs and is to take delivery of a further two 400Fs in August and November this year.
It also operates four Boeing 747-200Fs, including one on leaseback.
Globally, Cargolux transported 233,914 tonnes of airfreight last year, a rise of 7.8 percent on 1995.
Cargolux' 1996 figures also showed aircraft utilisation per 747F, expressed in block hours per day, had been reduced on the previous year's levels.
Last year, the Luxembourg carrier's 747-200Fs recorded 12.43 hours per day compared to 14.13 hours in 1995 while its 747-400Fs recorded 14.86 hours down from 15.56 hours in 1995.

"The reduction in block hours was largely due to having one extra aircraft in service than in 1995 a 200 version and also to the fact that in the early months of 1996 we had operated fewer frequencies to the Far East, a Cargolux official told Reuters.
Cargolux operates 21 scheduled weekly flights from Europe to North America, 16 to the Asia/Pacfic sector, 15 to the Near and Middle East and two to South Africa, Cargolux said.
Global revenues totalled $397 million compared to $389 million in 1995. --Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542-7706 Fax+44 171 542-5017
